stem:
If $X = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, $Y = \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$ and $Z = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$ are matrices, then which of the following is/ are possible for matrix multiplication?
I. $XY$
II. $XZ$
III. $ZY$
explanation: Orders: $X$ is $2\times 2$, $Y$ is $2\times 1$, $Z$ is $1\times 2$. $XY$ is $(2\times 2)(2\times 1) \rightarrow 2\times 1$ (valid). $XZ$ is $(2\times 2)(1\times 2)$ (columns $\neq$ rows, invalid). $ZY$ is $(1\times 2)(2\times 1) \rightarrow 1\times 1$ (valid). Thus I and III are possible. Current Grade X.
answer_origin: Official key cross-checked; explanations are supplementary
